tools.name: upload_file
tools.description: Publish a file and get a public Link in Seconds URL that opens in any browser (no sign-in for the viewer). Pass the file as text in `content` (HTML, Markdown, CSV, SVG, JSON...) or as base64 in `content_base64` (PDF, images, ZIP...). Up to 3 MB; for bigger files use create_upload_url. The account's

tools.name: create_upload_url
tools.description: For files too big to send inline: returns a one-time upload URL (valid 10 minutes). PUT the raw file bytes to it with the given Content-Type header (for example with curl), then call finish_upload with the returned path.

tools.name: finish_upload
tools.description: Call after PUTting the file to the URL from create_upload_url. Checks and scans the file, then returns its public link.

tools.name: list_links
tools.description: List the links on this Link in Seconds account, newest first, with their URLs and status.

tools.name: get_link_analytics
tools.description: Read-only. How one of the account's links performed: views, unique visitors, time on the file, how far readers got (pages for PDFs, watch-through for video and audio, scroll depth for pages), countries, devices, traffic sources and the busiest hour, over a UTC window. tools.name: get_account_analytics
tools.description: Read-only. The whole account's analytics over a UTC window: views, unique visitors, time on files, countries, devices, traffic sources, busiest hour and the top links.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: upload_file, list_links, get_link_analytics · Private data: upload_file, create_upload_url, finish_upload, get_link_analytics, get_account_analytics · Public sink: upload_file, create_upload_url, finish_upload.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: upload_file, list_links, get_link_analytics · Private data: upload_file, create_upload_url, finish_upload, get_link_analytics, get_account_analytics · Public sink: upload_file, create_upload_url, finish_upload

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
